transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2025-08-27 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (CSM), Priya (SE), Carlos (Ashbridge VP Eng), Aisha (Infra), Tom (PM), Leila (Sec)

Summary (auto): Kickoff focused on networking and security prerequisites for staging, decision to start with Redwood Hosted sandbox while evaluating Dedicated for production, and a follow-up SE deep-dive for benchmarking.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we can get started. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. With me are Ethan our CSM and Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: Good, thanks Maya. Excited to kick this off, got a bunch of people from infra and product here.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: Hi, yeah Aisha here. We're mostly focused on networking and security constraints up front.
[00:23] Tom Reed: Tom from product, will be the PM for the integration.
[00:26] Leila Park: Leila, security architect. We'll ask a lot of questions about data residency and audit logs.
[00:31] Ethan Zhou: Quick intro from me — I'll be shepherding the onboarding and runbook follow-ups, and we'll coordinate the checkpoints.
[00:36] Priya Menon: And I'm Priya — I do the SE heavy lifting, benchmarks, runtime tuning, that sort of thing.
[00:42] Maya Patel: Awesome. Agenda for today: 1) clarify primary success criteria and timeline, 2) review deployment options and recommended initial path, 3) walk through the security and infra checklist, 4) plan next steps and owners.
[00:55] Carlos Mendes: Our main thing — we want a low-latency endpoint for customer-facing features and we need predictable cost. Timeline is target MVP in 8 weeks, can be flexible but would like to be realistic.
[01:10] Maya Patel: Great — latency, cost, timeline — noted. Priya, do you want to briefly call out the typical tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private for a setup like Ashbridge's?
[01:20] Priya Menon: Sure — hosted is fastest to get started, lower operational overhead; you pay per usage and we provide metrics. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and flat commits, better for consistent traffic patterns. Private/VPC is for data controls — you manage the network peering and we deploy the runtime inside your VPC or via a private endpoint. For latency-sensitive customer-facing features, Dedicated or Private usually wins if you can commit to capacity, but hosted sandbox is fine for early ramp and testing.
[01:46] Aisha Khan: Quick clarifying question on VPC — if we do private, do we need to open inbound ports? We have strict egress rules.
[01:54] Priya Menon: Good question. For VPC peering we primarily need egress for control-plane callbacks and logs; inbound is typically limited to our management plane during setup. We'll provide a peering checklist. There can be some back-and-forth with your network team but no wide open inbound holes.
[02:10] Leila Park: And about audit logs — do you retain detailed token-level requests? We need to satisfy our internal audit and potentially SOC2 evidence.
[02:18] Ethan Zhou: We can retain token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route traces and request logs. There's an enterprise package for longer retention and encrypted log exports to your S3 or SIEM; we'll include our security pack in the follow-up.
[02:34] Tom Reed: On SSO, we use SAML via Okta — what's the flow for user provisioning?
[02:40] Maya Patel: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll need your IdP metadata file; we'll walk you through the SSO setup in staging.
[02:48] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. On the benchmarks piece — what metrics do you usually collect for production readiness?
[02:54] Priya Menon: Latency p50/p95, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens, cold-start behavior if any, and model regression checks for quality. For customer-facing, we recommend p95 < 300ms for short prompts, but that depends on model and sequence length. We'll tailor targets with you.
[03:16] [03:16] Carlos Mendes: p95 < 300ms — okay that's tight but good target.
[03:20] Aisha Khan: We also need to know about network egress costs — if you're routing via a region that costs more, we need visibility into that.
[03:27] Ethan Zhou: We provide token-level and region-level cost breakdowns in Console; we'll include sample reports.
[03:33] Maya Patel: Quick check — for MVP, are you open to starting in Hosted sandbox while we run benchmarks? Or do you need Dedicated from day one?
[03:41] Carlos Mendes: Hosted sandbox is fine for now, as long as we can mirror production-like latency in benchmarks to validate Dedicated later.
[03:49] Tom Reed: Also want canary rollouts and feature flags for prompt changes.
[03:53] Priya Menon: We have rollout tooling: canary routes, A/B variants, automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained. We'll show that in the SE deep-dive.
[04:05] [04:05] Aisha Khan: About encryption — keys at rest and KMS options? We need customer-managed keys if on Private, right?
[04:12] Ethan Zhou: Correct — for Private or enterprise Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys for storage.
[04:19] Leila Park: Any certifications or SOC stuff we can review?
[04:22] Maya Patel: We'll attach our SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO references in the security pack.
[04:27] [04:27] (brief crosstalk)
[04:30] Priya Menon: Moving into tenant mapping — how many logical environments do you want? Typical approach is staging sandbox tenant, pre-prod test tenant, and prod tenant. For multi-team companies you can have sub-tenants. What's your preference?
[04:45] Carlos Mendes: We want at least staging and prod. We may create a separate tenant per product line later.
[04:51] Priya Menon: OK, we'll create an initial staging tenant for Ashbridge and provision the sandbox API keys.
[04:56] Maya Patel: We'll need a list of people who need access and their roles for RBAC. Tom, can you own the user list?
[05:03] Tom Reed: Yep I can do that — I'll send a spreadsheet with names and roles.
[05:07] Priya Menon: On the sandbox, we'll stand up an environment with sample prompts, also a small workload generator so you can see p50/p95 under light load. For production perf we can run larger synthetic loads in the deep-dive.
[05:21] [05:21] Carlos Mendes: How do you handle rate limiting and burst capacity? We might have traffic spikes.
[05:26] Priya Menon: We have rate limits per-token and per-route; Dedicated has configurable burst policies and autoscaling. For hosted we have soft rate limits and we can work with you on quotas for the sandbox to test spikes.
[05:38] Maya Patel: Let's talk about data retention and logs — Leila, any strict retention requirements?
[05:44] Leila Park: We need logs for 13 months and the ability to export logs to our SIEM. Also strict PII filtering before logs leave our environment, if possible.
[05:54] Ethan Zhou: We can push logs to your S3 with customer-managed encryption and configurable retention. For PII filtering, we have options: redaction hooks and a post-processing step before export. We'll include those details in the security pack.
[06:10] [06:10] (brief pause)
[06:14] Carlos Mendes: Regarding model choices — do you recommend any specific open models for our use case? We're leaning toward a smaller 7B for initial cost control.
[06:22] Priya Menon: That makes sense. We can start with a 7B quantized profile for cost and evaluate quality. If you need higher quality, we can recommend a 13B or 70B variant and measure cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll include model recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[06:38] Aisha Khan: One last infra question — do we need a VPN or just VPC peering?
[06:43] Priya Menon: VPC peering or PrivateLink typically works; VPN is optional if you need an overlay. We'll send specific network options in the checklist.
[06:52] Maya Patel: Great. Timebox check — we have about 35 minutes left, want to move into the runbook walkthrough and show the key artifacts we'll hand over, and then capture owners.
[07:02] [07:02] Maya Patel: (shares screen) The onboarding runbook includes: access and credentials, SSO setup, VPC peering checklist, sample prompts and evaluation harness, and a benchmarking plan. Link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/ashbridge (will send real link).
[07:18] Carlos Mendes: Can you show the benchmarking section?
[07:21] Priya Menon: Sure — benchmark has three phases: 1) correctness/quality evals with your prompt set, 2) latency and throughput with synthetic traffic, 3) regression monitoring once we roll out. We'll ask for a representative prompt set and expected output examples.
[07:40] Tom Reed: For quality evals, can we add our own scoring rubric?
[07:44] Priya Menon: Absolutely, we support custom evals and alerting thresholds on regressions.
[07:49] [07:49] (minor audio glitch)
[07:52] Leila Park: About regulations — we have EU residents data and need to make sure any processing stays in EU for certain datasets. How do you support region restrictions?
[07:59] Ethan Zhou: We can pin deployments to region and provide region-aware routing. For Private deployments you can choose our EU region or on-prem options.
[08:07] Carlos Mendes: Ok good.
[08:10] Maya Patel: Capture a couple commitments — Redwood: send runbook and security pack by next Tuesday, SE to draft benchmark plan, and Ashbridge provide infra diagram + IdP metadata.
[08:22] [08:22] Aisha Khan: We'll get the infra diagram ready — expect some follow-up questions after you send the checklist.
[08:28] Tom Reed: I'll compile the initial user list and sample prompts.
[08:31] Priya Menon: I'll start drafting the benchmark plan and include a small synthetic load script for staging.
[08:36] [08:36] Maya Patel: Great — next steps and owners are in the notes. Anything else before we open for Qs?
[08:42] Carlos Mendes: One question — any additional cost associated with longer log retention for enterprise?
[08:47] Ethan Zhou: Yes, add-on for extended retention, but we can provide an initial estimate with the security pack.
[08:54] Leila Park: Also can you confirm SSO provisioning cadence — expected lead time?
[08:58] Maya Patel: Once we have IdP metadata and user list, SSO typically takes 2-3 business days to configure in staging.
[09:05] [09:05] (some typing/background noise)
[09:12] Priya Menon: Quick note on rollout strategy — recommend canary with 10% traffic, monitor p95 and error rate, then 50/50, then full. That usually mitigates risk for prompt changes.
[09:26] Tom Reed: Perfect.
[09:28] Maya Patel: Ok let's do lightning round Qs:
[09:31] Aisha Khan: Will we have direct support for peering issues?
[09:34] Ethan Zhou: Yes, SE + infra team will assist during peering, and we can set up a direct slack channel for support during the peering window.
[09:42] Carlos Mendes: Who is our main contact should incidents happen in prod?
[09:45] Ethan Zhou: Ethan (CSM) is primary for coordination, Priya for technical escalation, and Maya for commercial/scope. We'll set on-call paths in the runbook.
[09:58] [09:58] (short pause)
[10:02] Leila Park: Anything about data erasure requests? Need to ensure we can delete customer data on demand.
[10:07] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we support deletion requests and audit trails; we'll include process in security pack.
[10:14] Maya Patel: Alright friends, final recap: Redwood to send runbook + security docs by Tue 2025-09-02; Ashbridge to provide infra diagram and SSO metadata by Fri 2025-09-05; SE deep-dive scheduled week of 2025-09-08 (Priya to propose times). Action owners in notes.
[10:34] Carlos Mendes: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[10:36] Tom Reed: Thanks.
[10:38] Aisha Khan: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:40] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links and owners.

Auto-detected action items: Maya to send runbook, Priya to provide benchmark plan, Aisha/Carlos to share infra diagrams and SSO metadata, Tom to share user list and prompts.

References mentioned: onboarding runbook (will be emailed), security pack (SOC2 summary), sample benchmark harness (SE will share), link placeholder: https://redwood.example/runbooks/ashbridge

End of transcript.
